summary: **For Petitioner** : Shri Anand K. Ganeshan, Advocate, STPL Shri Vidhan Vyas, Advocate, STPL - _“a) Admit the Petition and grant approval to the Petitioner for establishment of permanent Transmission Line Stores along with associated infrastructure as proposed in the petition hereinabove;_ - _b) Permit the Petitioner to claim the additional capitalization incurred for the establishment of permanent Transmission Line Stores along with associated infrastructure on actual basis in the truing up exercise;_ - _c) The filing fee paid by the Petitioner in Petition No. 226/MP/2023 may be permitted to be adjusted towards the fee to be paid by the Petitioner for the instant petition._ - _d) Pass such other relief as Hon'ble Commission deems fit and appropriate under the circumstances of the case and in the interest of justice.”_ 3. The Petitioner had earlier filed Petition No. 226/MP/2023 for the grant of approval for the establishment of TLS and to claim the additional capitalisation incurred for the establishment of TLS on an actual basis at the time of truing-up under the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2019 (2019 Tariff Regulations). On the Petitioner's request, the Commission allowed the Petitioner to withdraw the said petition, with liberty to file a fresh petition in terms of the 2024 Tariff Regulations, vide order dated 10.5.2024 in Petition No. 226/MP/2023. Accordingly, the Petitioner has filed the instant petition seeking approval for the establishment of TLS and the consequent expenditure under Regulation 25 of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. 4. The gist of the submissions made by the Petitioner in support of its claims are as follows: h. The Petitioner was not able to procure land for establishing a permanent store during the construction of the Project due to financial constraints, and after commissioning of the Project due to the COVID-19 pandemic. or projected to be incurred within the original scope of work and after the cutoff date, after a prudence check. 5. The matter was heard on 26.11.2024, and notice was issued to the Respondents on the issue of maintainability. However, none of the Respondents filed any reply. 6. During the hearing on 8.5.2025, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the instant petition is maintainable since the claims regarding ACE fall within the original scope of the work, although these claims are being raised after the cut-off date, and this is in accordance with the provisions of Regulations 25(1) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. He further submitted that Regulation 25(1)(b) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations, recognise ‘change in law or compliance with any existing law’ with respect to ACE incurred or projected to be incurred within the original scope and after the cut-off date in respect of an existing project or a new project while the corresponding provision under Regulation 25(1)(b) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations provides ‘change in law or compliance with any existing law which is not provided for in the original scope of work’ in respect of ACE incurred or projected to be incurred in respect of an existing project or a new project. Referring to the above inconsistency between the 2019 Tariff Regulations and the 2024 Tariff Regulations, the Petitioner placed reliance on the case of H.S. Vankani and Ors. V. State of Gujarat and Ors [reported in (2010) 4 Supreme Court Cases 301], wherein the Hon’ble Supreme Court observed that the Courts have to avoid a construction of an enactment that leads to an unworkable, inconsistent or impracticable result, since such a situation is unlikely to have been envisaged by the rule-making authority. After hearing the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the order was reserved on maintainability, and the Respondents were given one more opportunity to file their reply on maintainability, and the Petitioner was given an opportunity to file a rejoinder, if any. Still, no reply has been filed by any of the Respondents. 7. We have considered the submissions made by the Petitioner on the maintainability of the petition. We examine the maintainability of the instant petition on the grounds of (a) jurisdiction, (b) cause of action, and (c) impermissibility under law. Regulations. We are of the view that the Petitioner has established a “cause of action” to consider the prayers made by the Petitioner on merit. 10. Further, the prayers made by the Petitioner in the instant petition are not barred by provisions of law. Therefore, the petition is maintainable on this count as well. 11. In view of the above, the instant petition is maintainable, and accordingly it is admitted. Issue notice to the Respondents. 12. The Petitioner is directed to serve a copy of the petition along with the enclosures on all 14 Respondents and file proof of service on affidavit within one week of the issue of this order. The Respondents are directed to file their reply by 28.1.2026 and the Petitioner to file its rejoinder, if any, by 11.2.2026. The parties are directed to adhere to the specified timelines and to complete the pleadings within the time allotted. Further, no extension of time shall be granted. 13. The petition shall be listed for hearing “on merits” in due course, and notice will be issued to the parties accordingly.
